questions.q: What is the main limitation of Azure's Bicep or AWS's CloudFormation compared to Terraform?
options: They only work with their own single cloud provider
They cannot be stored in version control
They require a paid license
They are not declarative
questions.explain: Bicep only talks to Azure and CloudFormation only talks to AWS, while Terraform works across many providers including both clouds at once.

questions.q: Why did a multi-cloud retailer like Northbridge Retail choose Terraform over Azure's and AWS's native tools?
options: One tool, one workflow, and one skillset could cover both of their clouds instead of maintaining two separate toolchains
Native cloud tools cannot create virtual machines
Terraform is the only free IaC tool
Terraform does not require any configuration files
questions.explain: Terraform's cloud-agnostic design let Northbridge standardize on a single workflow across both Azure and AWS, instead of learning and maintaining two separate tools.

questions.q: How does Pulumi differ from Terraform?
options: Pulumi is imperative, Terraform is declarative
Pulumi only works with on-premises infrastructure
Pulumi is configured using general-purpose programming languages instead of HCL
Pulumi cannot manage cloud resources
questions.explain: Pulumi is declarative like Terraform, but it's configured using languages like TypeScript, Python, or Go instead of Terraform's HCL.

questions.q: What job do tools like Ansible, Puppet, and Chef perform that is different from Terraform's job?
options: They are only used for billing and cost management
They provision new cloud resources from scratch
They replace the need for a cloud provider entirely
They configure software and settings inside a server that already exists
questions.explain: Configuration-management tools manage what runs inside an already-existing server, while Terraform's job is creating that server (and other infrastructure) in the first place.

options: It only works with on-premises data centers
It converts all infrastructure into a single universal cloud format
It refuses to work with any specific cloud provider
The same CLI, syntax, and workflow can target Azure, AWS, and hundreds of other providers through provider plugins
questions.explain: Terraform's provider plugin model means the same core tool and language can manage infrastructure across many different clouds and services.
